selection_rule: Disagreements first, then descending absolute score gap, then ascending ID

examples.inspection_note: A gendered insult overlays a political group photo. MPNet flags offensive wording; the supplied non-hateful label is ambiguous. Offensiveness and protected-group targeting require contextual interpretation.

examples.text: 72 virgins are ready to get fucked up
examples.inspection_note: A runway photo accompanies a vulgar caption about 72 virgins. MPNet may overreact to provocative wording without resolving its target; the supplied label is non-hateful and interpretation is context-dependent.

examples.text: when you decide to stop racism by burning its symbol
examples.inspection_note: The burning swastika identifies the symbol opposed by the anti-racist caption. MPNet may miss stance and cannot directly resolve the visual referent from the provided text.

examples.text: when you date an asian boy and you trynna get his family to accept you
examples.inspection_note: The image shows a woman playfully biting a dog's ear. Coupled with the caption about an Asian boyfriend's family, it invokes a racist dog-eating stereotype. CLIP misses the cross-modal connection; the correct text prediction may instead reflect lexical shortcuts.

examples.text: when your jewish friend smells a stash of coins in public
examples.inspection_note: An altered-nose portrait and a caption about a Jewish friend finding coins invoke antisemitic stereotypes. CLIP misses their combination; MPNet can exploit explicit lexical cues without inspecting the image.

interpretation_limit: Hypotheses from visual inspection, not model feature attribution. Supplied labels retained; selected cases are not representative error frequencies.
